results.summary_before: This project implements a shift register that loads a 6-bit input and shifts it out while encoding the bits for display. The write_not_shift control selects between loading and shifting, and the encoded bits are shown one at a time on an 8-segment display with the decimal point indicating the clock. It is tested using the standard Tiny Tapeout board with DIP switches for input and a display for output. The design is a simple demonstration of shift register and encoding logic.
results.summary: This project implements a driver for a 16x16 P10 LED panel, initially displaying the string TT03. It provides a 600 baud UART input to paint pixels, erase pixels, clear the display, and change the displayed colour. The design supports a single colour at a time, has no double buffer, and exhibits some flicker due to the low refresh rate. A mode pin allows selection between two different clocking patterns.

results.summary: This design is a simple tapped delay line with instrumentation. It uses a chain of inverters that is sampled at different stages, with edge detection to find the rising edge and a bank of flip-flops to sample eight sequential rising edge values. A UART interface at 9600 baud provides commands to shift data in and out, take a full 32-bit sample, or capture eight samples at a 25 MHz sample rate. The design is intended for measuring delay variations due to process, voltage, and temperature.
